rows.description: A child hides behind a parent at a party, whispers answers and joins play only after watching. Wants friends but needs time; pushing to say hello often deepens the freeze.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Wanting to join but holding back [Actor]
rows.description: A child longs to be part of the game yet waits to be invited and worries about saying the wrong thing. Warm-up time and a friendly bridge from a peer usually help, and shyness eases with safe practice.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: anxiety, shyness, trust

rows.description: A child called shy by everyone starts to believe it is who they are. Adults who avoid labels and instead praise small brave steps help the child feel capable rather than defective.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: shyness

rows.description: A teenager avoids answering in class, skips events and rehearses sentences for hours because of a strong fear of embarrassment. It differs from shyness in intensity and avoidance that shrinks life, and calls for support.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22
related mind states: fear, embarrassment, shyness
related concepts: avoidance

rows.description: Before speaking, a teenager feels a racing heart, blushing and a blank mind, and later replays every moment as a failure. Avoiding brings relief today but makes the fear larger, and gentle exposure with help works better.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22
related mind states: fear, relief

rows.description: A wise friend invites without pressure, speaks for quiet moments when asked, and celebrates small steps. Does not force the person to perform, and gently suggests seeing a professional if fear is stopping normal life.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22
related mind states: fear

rows.description: A young adult is quiet with strangers, enjoys small groups and does not suffer much about it. Being reserved is a temperament, not a problem to fix, and depth in a few friendships can be a strength.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17
related mind states: anger, shyness

rows.description: A student skips seminars, eats alone and turns down group work because being watched feels unbearable. Loneliness builds and self-criticism grows; seeking a counsellor early makes a real difference.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17
related mind states: loneliness

rows.description: A toddler explores, checks back with a caregiver, protests at parting and is soothed on return. Trust that comfort will come lets the child venture out, and feelings can be shown openly.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: trust

rows.subtype: Child who seeks comfort and returns to play [Actor]
rows.description: A child who is hurt runs to a parent, cries, is calmed and goes back to playing. Believes people will help, and tells a trusted adult about problems without much fear of blame.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: fear, calm, trust, hurt
